questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of sparse checkout?
options: Sparse checkout controls which paths are populated in the working tree; it does not remove excluded files from history. Select patterns carefully and test builds and editor tooling in the reduced checkout.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Sparse checkout controls which paths are populated in the working tree; it does not remove excluded files from history. Select patterns carefully and test builds and editor tooling in the reduced checkout.
questions.explanation: Sparse checkout controls which paths are populated in the working tree; it does not remove excluded files from history. Select patterns carefully and test builds and editor tooling in the reduced checkout.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git sparse-checkout list` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with sparse checkout?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
